defects.title: One WebSocket client can crash the whole server process (oversize frame)
defects.spec: docs/10 T11 (connection flood, send-buffer caps), NFR-AVAIL
defects.steps: 1. Obtain a ticket for any project you can read (a VIEWER suffices). 2. Open the socket. 3. Send one 1 MB text message.
defects.expected: The offending socket is closed (1009) and every other connection and tenant keeps being served.
defects.actual: The ws library emits an unhandled "error" event (WS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE_LENGTH, maxPayload 4096), the Node process exits with code 1, and every tenant loses service. Any authenticated user of any tenant can do this. Evidence: server stderr tail captured in the failing test.

defects.title: Audit hash chain does not cover actor, action, resource or time: rewriting them is undetected
defects.spec: docs/10 §7 and T13 (hash = SHA256(prev_hash || canonical_json(row)); any break pinpoints the first tampered row)
defects.steps: 1. As superuser disable the append-only trigger. 2. UPDATE audit_event SET actor_id / action / resource_id / occurred_at on one row. 3. Re-enable the trigger. 4. GET /audit-events/verify.
defects.expected: ok:false with firstBrokenId equal to the modified row (as it is for a modified detail column, which IS detected).
defects.actual: verify returns ok:true for all four columns, so the trail can be rewritten to blame someone else or hide who did what without detection. Only the detail column and row deletion/relinking are covered by the hash.

defects.title: assignment_timephase partitions have no row-level security; pf_app can read other tenants' rows through them
defects.spec: docs/10 T2 (RLS on every table, tested), docs/05
defects.steps: 1. As superuser insert timephase rows for tenant A and B. 2. As pf_app with NO tenant set (or tenant B) SELECT from pf.assignment_timephase_p0..p3.
defects.expected: Zero rows (RLS forced on every tenant table).
defects.actual: All rows of all tenants are returned from the partitions (the parent table is protected, the child partitions are not). Latent: the current server populates no timephase rows and queries only the parent, so it is not reachable through the API today.

defects.title: POST /resources accepts a calendarId belonging to another tenant (cross-tenant reference and existence oracle)
defects.steps: 1. As tenant B POST /resources {name, calendarId: <tenant A calendar id>}. 2. Repeat with a random uuid.
defects.expected: Both are rejected identically (400 unknown calendar / 404), nothing is stored.
defects.actual: The foreign id is accepted (201) and stored, the random id gets 400, so tenant B can test whether a given uuid is a tenant-A calendar (FK checks bypass RLS).

defects.title: Foreign keys are not tenant-composite: pf_app can insert a task whose project belongs to another tenant
defects.steps: 1. As pf_app with tenant B set, INSERT a task with project_id of a tenant-A project and tenant_id = B.
defects.expected: Rejected by a composite FK / check.
defects.actual: Accepted (RLS WITH CHECK only validates the row's own tenant_id).

defects.title: The last PROJECT_MANAGER can be demoted through PUT /members (only DELETE is guarded)
defects.steps: 1. Project with a single PM. 2. PM does PUT /members/{self} {role: VIEWER}.
defects.expected: 409/422: a project must keep a project manager.
defects.actual: 200: the project is left without anyone who can manage it.

defects.title: A PROJECT_MANAGER can demote or remove an ORG_ADMIN member
defects.spec: docs/10 §4 (members: ORG_ADMIN and PM; ORG_ADMIN grant restricted)
defects.steps: 1. ORG_ADMIN is a member (SQL-provisioned). 2. PM PUTs a lower role or DELETEs that member.
defects.expected: Refused: granting ORG_ADMIN needs an ORG_ADMIN, so removing one should as well.
defects.actual: PUT 200 and DELETE 204. Privilege inversion; the spec is silent, so reported as S3 / ambiguity.

defects.title: Access attempts by non-members (404) are not audited
defects.steps: 1. A tenant user who is not a member of a project repeatedly requests it. 2. Read the audit trail.
defects.expected: An audit event per denied access (as 403 denials get authz.denied).
defects.actual: Nothing is recorded for the 404 form of denial, so enumeration of project ids is invisible in the trail.

defects.title: 401 responses carry no WWW-Authenticate header
defects.steps: 1. GET /projects without a token.
defects.expected: WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ...
defects.actual: Header absent.

defects.title: Unauthenticated requests are never rate limited
defects.steps: 1. Send 200 requests without credentials in a minute.
defects.expected: A per-IP limit (429) is documented practice for anonymous traffic.
defects.actual: Always 401; no throttle. The specification only defines limits per tenant/user.

defects.title: Audit trail does not record authentication events
defects.steps: 1. Send a valid and an invalid-token request. 2. Read the audit trail.
defects.expected: Authentication events (at least failures) are recorded.
defects.actual: Only mutations and 403 denials are recorded.

defects.title: Server errors (500) for malformed but client-caused input
defects.steps: POST /resources {"name":"\u0000"}; PATCH /projects name NUL; addTask kind FIXED_WORK without workMin; constraint date 2026-13-09T08:00:00 or T25:00:00; estimate optimistic > likely; project name with a lone surrogate; GET /projects/% ; startDate 2026-02-31.
defects.expected: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for each.
defects.actual: INTERNAL 500 (database check-constraint, invalid-date and encoding errors leak through as 500). No stack or SQL is exposed, but clients cannot distinguish them from outages.

defects.title: Impossible calendar dates are silently accepted (2026-02-30)
defects.steps: addTask with constraint {type: SNET, date: "2026-02-30T08:00:00"}.
defects.expected: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.
defects.actual: 200: the date is normalised (rolls into March) without notice.

defects.title: Batch limits answered with 400, and the 2 MB body limit is not enforced
defects.steps: 1. POST 1001 commands. 2. POST a 3 MB body.
defects.expected: 413 PLAN_TOO_LARGE for both.
defects.actual: 1001 commands -> 400 VALIDATION_FAILED ("at most 1000"); a 3 MB body is parsed and validated field by field (no 413 at all).

defects.title: Stale resource cache: a resource created after the plan was first loaded cannot be assigned on the first attempt
defects.steps: 1. Create a project and a task. 2. POST /resources. 3. Immediately addAssignment with the new resource id.
defects.actual: 400 "unknown resource" on the first attempt; a retry succeeds. Every client that creates a resource and assigns it hits this.

defects.title: POST /resources rejects stdRatePerHour, so rates cannot be set; resource responses deviate from the contract
defects.steps: 1. POST /resources {"name":"x","stdRatePerHour":50}. 2. GET /resources.
defects.expected: 201 with the rate stored; list items valid against Resource.
defects.actual: 400 (unknown key); the create response omits calendarId and the list returns calendarId:null (schema violation). Cost EVM can only be exercised by SQL-provisioned rates.

defects.title: previewSchedule rejects the documented CommandBatch body
defects.steps: POST /projects/{id}/schedule {clientOpId, expectedPlanVersion, commands}.
defects.expected: 200 with a schedule preview.
defects.actual: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED (unknown keys clientOpId/expectedPlanVersion); only a bare {commands} body works.

defects.title: Several response bodies deviate from their OpenAPI schemas (list wrappers, load, scenario, baseline)
defects.steps: Call each operation and validate the body with ajv against api/openapi.yaml.
defects.expected: Arrays as documented; load = [{day, plannedMin, capacityMin, overallocated}]; Scenario.result has tasks; Baseline.savedAt.
defects.actual: Lists are wrapped as {items:[...]}; resource load is {resourceId, maxUnits, days:[{day, workMin, ...}]}; scenario result lacks tasks; saveBaseline response lacks savedAt.

defects.title: EVM response deviates from the contract (statusDate required, datetime, ac/cv null, no eac/etc)
defects.steps: GET /evm without statusDate; GET /evm?statusDate=2026-11-10.
defects.expected: 200 for the optional parameter; ac, cv numbers; statusDate formatted as date.
defects.actual: 400 when statusDate is omitted; statusDate returned as a datetime; ac and cv are null (actual cost "not tracked"); eac/etc/vac/tcpi absent.

defects.title: EVM ignores the baseline parameter
defects.steps: 1. Save baseline 1, change fixedCost. 2. GET /evm?baseline=1 and ?baseline=7.
defects.expected: baseline=1 uses the saved snapshot; baseline=7 (absent) -> 404.
defects.actual: Both answered from the live plan (BAC 5000 instead of 1000; baseline=7 returns 200).

defects.title: Saving a baseline number twice silently overwrites it (not immutable)
defects.steps: POST /baselines {number:1} twice with a plan edit between.
defects.expected: 409 on the second save; the first snapshot stays.
defects.actual: 201 again with a new planVersion/finish: the earlier baseline is replaced, destroying the reference for variance reporting.

defects.title: A baseline saved on an empty plan is not returned by listBaselines
defects.steps: Save baseline on a project with no tasks, then list.
defects.expected: One baseline listed.

defects.title: PATCH /projects rejects deadline
defects.steps: PATCH /projects/{id} {"deadline":"2026-12-01T17:00:00"}.
defects.actual: 400 (unknown key); a deadline can only be set through the setProject command.

defects.title: If-Match is not enforced on PATCH /projects
defects.steps: PATCH without If-Match.

defects.title: Task list filters q, critical and finishBefore are ignored
defects.steps: GET /tasks?q=..., ?critical=true, ?finishBefore=...
defects.expected: Filtered result.
defects.actual: Unfiltered list (only parentId works).

defects.title: Pagination is not implemented (cursor/limit ignored, limit=0 accepted)
defects.steps: GET /tasks?limit=3 on a 10-task project; GET /projects?limit=0.
defects.expected: Three tasks and a nextCursor; limit=0 -> 400.
defects.actual: All tasks, no nextCursor; limit=0 -> 200. (The performance suite shows the cost: GET /tasks?limit=100 returns 2,000 tasks.)

defects.title: Idempotency-Key header is ignored on POST /projects
defects.steps: POST /projects twice with the same Idempotency-Key (same body, then different body).
defects.expected: Same project returned; different body -> 409.
defects.actual: Two projects created / second accepted.

defects.title: Export format and Accept negotiation ignored
defects.steps: GET /export?format=csv; GET /plan with Accept: application/x-ndjson.
defects.expected: CSV / NDJSON; unknown format -> 400.
defects.actual: Always the JSON plan.

defects.title: 405 responses have the wrong body and no Allow header
defects.steps: GET /projects/{id}/members/{uid}.
defects.expected: 405 + Allow + problem.status 405.
defects.actual: 405 with body status 400 / VALIDATION_FAILED and no Allow header.

defects.title: Typed query parameters are not validated (garbage uuid/date accepted)
defects.steps: GET /audit-events?actorId=not-a-uuid&from=yesterday; GET /resources/{id}/load with from>to, missing from/to, 2026-02-31.
defects.expected: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.
defects.actual: 200 (filters silently ignored or empty result).

defects.title: Empty request body accepted where the contract requires one
defects.steps: POST /schedule and POST /baselines with an empty body.
defects.actual: 200 / 201 (a baseline is saved with a defaulted number).

defects.title: Changing nearCriticalMin does not recompute nearCritical flags; incremental state diverges from a full recompute
defects.steps: 1. Plan with a task having 480 min of float. 2. setProject nearCriticalMin 240. 3. GET plan.
defects.expected: nearCritical false (480 > 240); identical to what a fresh replay of the same plan produces.
defects.actual: nearCritical stays true until the process restarts and the plan is reloaded; the replay oracle shows the difference after a random edit sequence containing nearCriticalMin changes.

defects.title: A summary task can be critical and nearCritical at the same time
defects.steps: Plan with summaries; read a summary with totalFloatMin 0.
defects.expected: nearCritical false when totalFloatMin = 0.
defects.actual: nearCritical true (rolled up as any(child.nearCritical)) while totalFloatMin 0 and critical true.

defects.title: False MSO_VIOLATED when the pinned date is a non-working instant that maps to the same working position
defects.steps: Task with MSO 2026-11-11T17:00:00 (end of day) after one predecessor.
defects.expected: No conflict: the pinned start (next working minute) is not earlier than the predecessor push.
defects.actual: MSO_VIOLATED reported although the task is exactly where it was pinned (raw wall-clock compare against the normalised start). Dates are right; only the conflict list is wrong.

defects.title: WebSocket protocol deviates from docs/07 §6 and asyncapi.yaml
defects.steps: Connect, apply batches, observe messages.
defects.expected: hello {lastSeq}; plan.changed {seq, planVersion, actorId, clientOpId, commands}; schedule.delta.
defects.actual: hello has only projectId; plan.changed carries {projectId, planVersion, changedTaskIds}; no seq (gap detection impossible), no clientOpId (optimistic reconciliation impossible), no schedule.delta.

defects.title: Realtime ticket lives 30 s although docs and OAS say 60 s
defects.steps: POST /realtime/tickets and compare expiresAt.
defects.actual: 30 s (documentation and implementation disagree).

defects.title: A maximum-size risk run blocks the whole server: no per-tenant bulkhead; other tenants get connection resets
defects.spec: docs/10 T12 (per-tenant concurrency bulkhead), T20 (noisy neighbour), NFR-SCAL
defects.steps: 1. Tenant A: 2,000-task plan, POST /risk-runs {iterations:2000}. 2. 0.7 s later tenant B (fresh connection): GET /projects/{id}.
defects.expected: Tenant B answered < 5 s; the risk run is queued/limited per tenant.
defects.actual: The risk run executes synchronously on the event loop for 20-50 s; tenant B request fails with ECONNRESET (the server drops the connection once its own header timeout elapses while the loop is blocked). Keep-alive connections were also reset. The server recovers afterwards.

defects.title: Killing a database backend while a request holds it crashes the whole server process (no error listener on checked-out clients)
defects.spec: NFR-REL (DB connection loss), NFR-AVAIL, docs/04 resilience
defects.steps: 1. Start server and send traffic. 2. SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) for the pf_app backends (or restart PostgreSQL / lower the role connection limit) while requests are in flight.
defects.expected: In-flight requests fail with 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; the process stays up and recovers.
defects.actual: Intermittent (a race: it needs the backend to die while a client is checked out between queries): the process exits with code 1 on an unhandled "error" event emitted by a pg Client (server/src/db.ts tx(): pool.on("error") covers only idle clients; the checked-out PoolClient has no listener). All tenants lose service until a supervisor restarts it. Reproduced in 1 of 3 full runs; earlier runs passed.
